A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QRGCL jet-discrimination work and are readable throughout. v1 has no appendix; v2's Appendices A–F largely retain material moved from v1's main text, alongside identifiable additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original quark–gluon classification experiments, hyperparameter comparisons, ablations, and training curves in Tables I–III and Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–3 and Figure 5, with detailed discussion in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The quantum circuit, ParticleNet pipeline, and weighted loss components are retained. However, Appendix C.2 replaces the unspecified pdist-based uniformity expression with an explicit squared-distance kernel and labels fidelity alignment theoretical while still saying it was used. The PDFs do not establish whether these revisions change the procedure or clarify earlier descriptions.

E1.justification: Both evaluate quark–gluon discrimination using the same Pythia8 jet dataset and collision conditions. Other applications remain cited examples or future directions; no additional dataset, task, or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding tables retain CRGCL, GNN, EGNN, QGNN, EQGNN, QCL, CQCL, three QCGCL encoding variants, and the RX+H QRGCL variant. Newly cited methods, including Lorentz-EQGNN, are not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: The 12,500-jet sample, 10,000/1,250/1,250 split, preprocessing, evaluation metrics, and tabled model configurations and training budgets are unchanged. Appendix E retains v1's experimental settings rather than introducing a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: All tabulated encoding, entanglement, learning-rate, graph-size, depth, and augmentation ablations remain. However, v1's explicit observation that the uniformity component hindered learning becomes conditional advice about omitting it in Appendix C.2.3, weakening the reported evidence about that component's effect.

E5.justification: Both report 10-fold cross-validation and calculation of metric means and standard deviations. Table III/Table 3 retains the same uncertainty reporting; no additional seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are disclosed.

E6.justification: All percentage values in the three corresponding tables match exactly, including QRGCL's 77.53% ± 0.88% AUC, and Figure 5 retains the same curves. The limited change is qualitative: v1 reports that uniformity loss hindered learning, whereas v2 only conditionally discusses possible harm.

T1.justification: v1 provides loss formulas with short explanations. Appendix C.2 adds a Donsker–Varadhan-based InfoNCE derivation, an RA likelihood derivation, a pure-state fidelity relation, two theorems with proof sketches, and a bounded-gradient assertion. This substantially expands the mathematical treatment beyond relocated material.

C1.justification: v2's introduction explicitly presents the quantum-enhanced contrastive loss as a distinct novel contribution. The central framework, parameter-efficiency, jet-discrimination, and benchmark-outperformance claims remain, including the same headline AUC and 45-parameter QRG.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 adds interpretations involving alignment up to global phase and entropy preservation through uniformity, and conditionally frames fidelity alignment in terms of embeddings representing quantum states. The new Limitations section mostly relocates existing future work, adding Lorentz-EQGNN as a possible encoder.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code access link in the abstract, absent from v1. Hardware, software frameworks, preprocessing instructions, and most implementation and hyperparameter details are retained through relocation to the appendices.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 15 to 36 works, adding broad coverage of invariant and equivariant learning, recent graph and quantum contrastive methods, Lorentz-equivariant models, and explicit foundations for InfoNCE and alignment/uniformity. The underlying positioning as a quantum extension of classical RGCL remains.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative into main-text summaries and Appendices A–F covering background, preprocessing, architecture, baselines, settings, and results. It expands the loss exposition, replaces the introductory roadmap with contributions, and adds separate Broader Impacts and Limitations sections.

P2.justification: The two-column layout becomes a single-column preprint layout. Existing figure panels are resized and rearranged, notably Figures 2, 3, and 5. All three tables are redesigned and consolidated onto one page, with revised rules and directional arrows; the underlying figure images and table values are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds code-access information, broader citations, and more explicit loss explanations while retaining the empirical evidence. However, its new theory introduces internal inconsistencies: Theorem 1's proof treats RA as having a positive-inclusive denominator, although Equation 17 excludes the positive term. Fidelity alignment is also labeled theoretical while still described as used. These benefits and new reliability ambiguities prevent a confident net quality judgment.
